text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000216 bills 99215 far above the expected rate, mostly on low-complexity patients, yet the small set of returned charts largely documents high MDM, so the records neither confirm nor clear the pattern.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The claims pattern is consistent with upcoding: the 99215 share is elevated in every complexity stratum, not just among sicker patients, and most sampled 99215s are single-problem or acute visits such as C0111481 (J06.9 only) and C0111309 (R10.9 only). Against that, the documented 99215 claims mostly support the billed level, with only one below-billed case (C0111338), close to the comparison rate. That documentation rests on 17 charts from a small records return with no audit trail. The note signals suggest the charts may not reflect what happened: the problems flag appears on a large share of notes, some visit times repeat, and a few notes claim moderate-or-higher data review with no lab or test line on the claim. A reviewer should first read the flagged notes (C0111264, C0111314, C0111396, C0111404, C0111920) and the supported low-complexity 99215 C0111836 (depression with URI, high MDM, no time recorded) for cloned or templated content, then request more 99215 charts on 0–1 condition patients and the EHR audit trail."}
